items.title: The actual cosine feature matrix spans the block Krylov space

source.anchor: Section4.2 block Krylov definition S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2; AppendixC.2 FactC.5 range, A3.SS2.2 proof and A3.SS2.p19/inline Ex130–131 quadratic use

items.statement: For the literal affine cosine spectrum, the image of the normalized feature matrix is exactly the block Krylov space. Every Krylov vector therefore has one coefficient representation giving both Euclidean quadratic identities. \operatorname{range}(B)=K_q=\operatorname{span}\{\Lambda^j g_a:0\le a,j\le q\}. \(d,q\in\mathbb N\), \(2q+1<d\), and \(\kappa\ge2\). The case \(q=0\) is included; the dimension condition implies \(d\ge2\). Put \(r=q+1\), \(\theta_i=(i+1/2)\pi/d\), \(\lambda_i=(\kappa+1)/2+(\kappa-1)\cos\theta_i/2\), and \(\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i)\), with zero-based indices. The starts \(g_a\in\mathbb R^d\) are arbitrary deterministic vectors, encoded by \(x\in\mathbb R^{d\times r}\). They are unscaled. Define \(t_{i0}=1\), \(t_{ij}=\sqrt2\cos(j\theta_i)\) for \(j>0\), and \(B_{i,(a,j)}=d^{-1/2}(g_a)_i t_{ij}\). The space \(K_q\) is defined independently as the span of ordinary matrix powers \(\Lambda^j g_a\). No full-rank, vector-independence, Gaussian, polynomial-basis or normalization certificate is assumed. For the private application, \(D=\operatorname{diag}(\cos((2q+1)\theta_i))\). Norm and inner product are the real Euclidean ones, explicitly realized by \(\mathrm{WithLp.toLp}\ 2\).

formulae.label: The actual cosine feature image equals the Krylov span

assumptions: \(d,q\in\mathbb N\), \(2q+1<d\), and \(\kappa\ge2\). The case \(q=0\) is included; the dimension condition implies \(d\ge2\).

The starts \(g_a\in\mathbb R^d\) are arbitrary deterministic vectors, encoded by \(x\in\mathbb R^{d\times r}\). They are unscaled. Define \(t_{i0}=1\), \(t_{ij}=\sqrt2\cos(j\theta_i)\) for \(j>0\), and \(B_{i,(a,j)}=d^{-1/2}(g_a)_i t_{ij}\).

The space \(K_q\) is defined independently as the span of ordinary matrix powers \(\Lambda^j g_a\). No full-rank, vector-independence, Gaussian, polynomial-basis or normalization certificate is assumed.
For the private application, \(D=\operatorname{diag}(\cos((2q+1)\theta_i))\). Norm and inner product are the real Euclidean ones, explicitly realized by \(\mathrm{WithLp.toLp}\ 2\).

obligations.label: Actual image=Krylov equality, with a private same-witness Euclidean norm and weighted-inner application.

bindings.boundary: Pointwise range component of Appendix C.2 Fact C.5, and a private same-witness Euclidean quadratic-coordinate application underlying the proof of Lemma4.4. Arbitrary deterministic starts are a source-proof-supported strengthening of the Gaussian-context assertion; no Gaussian law or coefficient measurability is asserted. The signed bilinear identity is proved directly, not inferred by reversing an absolute-value equality. The separate cosine-frame Gram/mean results are not formal parents of range. Fact C.6 concentration, a source-valid absolute constant, full uniform Lemma4.4, deferred Haar/joint/adaptive/private-seed/transcript/output-law constructions, exact matvec/finite precision/TV and dimension-condition-number adapters, deterministic worst-query caps and explicit expected-cost comparisons, both main lower bounds, public integration, desktop/mobile delivery and postmerge purification/Exposition Seal remain open.

assumption_deltas.source: FactC.5 appears with independent Gaussian starting vectors in the Lemma4.4 setup.
assumption_deltas.lean: The exact range identity is pointwise for every deterministic starting array x; no law, rank or independence binder is added.
assumption_deltas.reason: The source polynomial change-of-coordinates proof is deterministic and works for any starts, even dependent or zero starts. The stochastic Lemma4.4 remains separate.

assumption_deltas.source: K_q is the span of ordinary powers of the actual diagonal spectrum applied to unscaled g_a; B alone has row scale d^(-1/2) and normalized cosine columns.
assumption_deltas.lean: Exactly these literal matrix powers, starts, column weights and nonzero row factor at kappa>=2 and2q+1<d, including q0.
assumption_deltas.reason: No span equality, basis, invertibility, normalization or concentration result is made a premise.

assumption_deltas.source: The Lemma4.4 proof uses u=Bc, the Euclidean norm and an absolute weighted quadratic equality.
assumption_deltas.lean: A private theorem obtains one existential c from the producer and proves the actual Euclidean norm square and signed weighted-inner identity simultaneously.
assumption_deltas.reason: The signed identity follows directly from bilinear matrix algebra and implies the displayed absolute identity; no converse inference from absolute values or measurable/random-coefficient selection is used.
